The function \(f(n)\) is defined as the value of the base-ten numeral of \(n\) interpreted in base \(b\), where \(b\) is the smallest integer greater than the greatest digit in \(n\). The goal is to find the number of positive integers \(n < 1000\) such that \(f(n) = n\).

For single-digit numbers (\(n = 1\) to \(9\)), the greatest digit is the number itself. Interpreting this single digit in base \(b\) (where \(b\) is one greater than the digit) gives the same numerical value as \(n\). Thus, \(f(n) = n\) for all single-digit numbers, and there are 9 such numbers.

For two-digit numbers (\(n = 10\) to \(99\)), the maximum digit is \(d_{\text{max}} = \max(a, b)\), where \(a\) is the tens digit (from 1 to 9) and \(b\) is the units digit (from 0 to 9), so \(b_{\text{base}} = d_{\text{max}} + 1\). The equation \(f(n) = n\) simplifies to \(a(b_{\text{base}}) + b = 10a + b\), leading to \(a(d_{\text{max}} + 1) = 10a\). Since \(a \neq 0\), this gives \(d_{\text{max}} + 1 = 10\), so \(d_{\text{max}} = 9\). Thus, \(f(n) = n\) if and only if the maximum digit is 9, which occurs when at least one digit is 9. The total number of two-digit numbers is 90. The number of two-digit numbers with no digit 9 is \(8 \times 9 = 72\) (tens digit from 1 to 8, units digit from 0 to 8). Thus, the number with at least one 9 is \(90 - 72 = 18\).

For three-digit numbers (\(n = 100\) to \(999\)), the maximum digit is \(d_{\text{max}} = \max(a, b, c)\), where \(a\) is the hundreds digit (from 1 to 9), and \(b\) and \(c\) are the tens and units digits (from 0 to 9), so \(b_{\text{base}} = d_{\text{max}} + 1\). The equation \(f(n) = n\) simplifies to \(a(b_{\text{base}})^2 + b \cdot b_{\text{base}} + c = 100a + 10b + c\), which, after rearrangement, shows that \(b_{\text{base}} = 10\) is required for equality (as \(b_{\text{base}} < 10\) results in \(f(n) < n\)). Since \(b_{\text{base}} = 10\) implies \(d_{\text{max}} = 9\), \(f(n) = n\) if and only if the maximum digit is 9, which occurs when at least one digit is 9. The total number of three-digit numbers is 900. The number of three-digit numbers with no digit 9 is \(8 \times 9 \times 9 = 648\) (hundreds digit from 1 to 8, tens and units digits from 0 to 8). Thus, the number with at least one 9 is \(900 - 648 = 252\).

The sets (one-digit, two-digit with digit 9, three-digit with digit 9) are disjoint, so the total is the sum: \(9 + 18 + 252 = 279\).

Alternatively, the numbers that do not satisfy \(f(n) = n\) are the multi-digit numbers with no digit 9. There are 72 two-digit and 648 three-digit such numbers, totaling \(72 + 648 = 720\). The total number of positive integers less than 1000 (i.e., 1 to 999) is 999. Thus, the number satisfying \(f(n) = n\) is \(999 - 720 = 279\).

Both methods confirm that the number of such positive integers is 279.

\boxed{279}
